rationale: Lycopolitan ⲕⲛⲓⲉ = Sah. ⲕⲛⲛⲉ 'fatness, sweetness, richness.' Listed alongside oil and milk as the maternal gathering-substances by which the cosmic Mother draws the captive light back.

Greek ἀναίρεσις 'taking-away, removal, lifting-up' (from ἀναιρέω). Used here for the eschatological extraction of all the Light mingled with Darkness — the upward gathering at the end of the Three Times.
Standard Coptic ⲧⲛⲧⲱⲛ/ⲥⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ in qualitative or relative form: 'that which is likened.' Used in correspondential parable construction.
Lycopolitan ⲧⲟⲓⲛ- (action-noun prefix) + ⲉⲓ 'come.' Functions as verbal noun 'the coming, the arrival.' Cf. parallel formation ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'the dissolution' in earlier vocabulary.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲁⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ/ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ = Sah. ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'awake, arouse.' Eschatological awakening of the gathered Light.
ⲣ̄- (do) + ⲃⲁⲗ (outside) + ⲁ- (directional 'to/from'). Restored idiomatic phrase for 'escape from one's hand.'
Standard Coptic ⲱⲡ 'count, number, reckon.' Used twice in this passage for the cosmic accounting of the gathered light-souls (line 14: ⲛϥⲧⲙ̄ⲱⲡ 'shall not be counted'; line 29: ⲟ̄ⲁⲡⲟⲩ 'reckon them').
